title: Node 22.18 breaks npm package because experimental strip-types is enabled
body: After updating from Node 22.17 to v22.18.0, our builds consistently fail on Linux, Windows, and Azure DevOps build agents. They run only if I add --no-experimental-strip-types to the Node command line. I expect an existing LTS line not to enable an experimental feature by default in a minor release.

symptoms_visible: Our CI builds consistently fail with Node 22.18.0 after working with Node 22.17.
The same builds run when I add --no-experimental-strip-types to the Node command line.
N0.label: N0 Node 22.18 CI regression reported

symptoms_visible: With Node 22.18, our tests suddenly report that __dirname is not defined even though we do not specify a type in our package.json files.
Adding --no-experimental-strip-types makes the tests run again.
N1.label: N1 concrete failure described

symptoms_visible: The project still fails without --no-experimental-strip-types, and I do not currently have an isolated example outside the large existing project.
N2.label: N2 reproduction constraints established

symptoms_visible: The tests fail on Node 22.18 without the opt-out flag, and I found that the project is using Mocha 10.
N3.label: N3 outdated test-runner dependency identified

symptoms_visible: After upgrading Mocha to the latest release, the original tests run on Node 22.18 without --no-experimental-strip-types.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter problem resolved by Mocha upgrade

question_patterns: What exact error do your builds produce on Node 22.18?
Can you describe the first concrete failure and the package module configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: What I saw was that __dirname was suddenly not defined. We do not specify type in our package.json files, so I expected the project to fall back to CommonJS. This worked through Node 22.17, and adding --no-experimental-strip-types makes it work again on 22.18.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failure is an out-of-memory crash before any test or module is loaded, and the flag does not change it.
The same __dirname error occurs, but only on one of our Linux CI agents.

edges.comment: Reporter chain from c1 and c3: participant1 requested the actual error and reproduction details; the reporter described the undefined __dirname symptom, absence of a package type, the version boundary, and the working opt-out flag on the reporter's own project.

question_patterns: Can you provide a small standalone reproduction of the failure?
Can you isolate the problem from the application into a minimal project?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I do not have access to the specific failing code right now, but I can investigate. This is one very large project that is about seven years old, so upgrades are not always easy. I have also seen the problem with Node 24.5.0.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can provide the same project logs tomorrow, but I still cannot share the proprietary source.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c3 and c9, responding to reproduction requests in c1 and c6: the reporter could not immediately isolate the proprietary large project and additionally volunteered that the same project had problems on Node 24.5. This remains the reporter's setup and is not merged with other participants' reproductions.

question_patterns: Which testing framework and version does this project use?
What dependencies in the project customize test or module loading?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I found that we use Mocha 10 in our project.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This project does not use Mocha or any custom test or module loader.
It uses a different patch release within Mocha 10.

edges.comment: Reporter message c19 follows participant8's c16 request to identify testing frameworks and module-loading customizations. Only the reporter's confirmed Mocha 10 dependency is folded into this chain; the separate ts-node, TSX, SWC, Jasmine, Jest, and node:test deployments belong to other participants.

solution.intent: Upgrade the reporter's old Mocha dependency to the latest supported release so its module-loading behavior is compatible with Node's default TypeScript handling, then rerun the original CI tests without the strip-types opt-out flag.
solution.concrete_example: Update Mocha to its latest release, remove NODE_OPTIONS=--no-experimental-strip-types for the verification run, and rerun the same test suite on Node 22.18. The reporter confirmed that this fixed the initial problem.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter established the version boundary, the working strip-types opt-out, use of Mocha 10, and successful upgrade. Maintainers connected this to older Mocha module-loading behavior not expecting Node to handle TypeScript by default. The thread analyzes a specific unsupported-TypeScript-error retry mechanism for another participant's reproduction, then warns that reproduction may differ from the reporter's; therefore that exact internal error path must not be asserted as proven for the reporter.

edges.comment: Resolution of the opening reporter's own chain from c15-c16 and c19-c20: upgrading Mocha was proposed as the best course for the old-Mocha reproduction, and the reporter personally confirmed that upgrading fixed the initial problem and removed the need for --no-experimental-strip-types. Later TSX, ts-node, SWC, Jasmine, Jest, and node:test reports are independent deployments and are deliberately excluded.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the reporter's accepted diagnosis at the supported level: Node 22.18's default TypeScript handling exposed a compatibility problem in the project's old Mocha 10 module-loading behavior.
Must ground the recommendation in the collected evidence: the project worked on Node 22.17, failed on 22.18, temporarily worked with --no-experimental-strip-types, and was found to use Mocha 10.
Must recommend upgrading Mocha as the reporter's durable fix; the strip-types opt-out may be mentioned as a temporary workaround but not as the final resolution.

Must not splice in the distinct TSX, ts-node, SWC, Jasmine, Jest, or node:test failures reported by other participants, nor claim their separate patches or mechanisms resolved the opening reporter's project.
Must ask the reporter to rerun the original tests on Node 22.18 without --no-experimental-strip-types and only treat the case as resolved after that verification succeeds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced application developer maintaining a large, seven-year-old project and CI across multiple platforms; comfortable changing Node flags and dependencies but initially unable to isolate a minimal reproduction.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and practical, with strong expectations about LTS stability; provides concise observations, acknowledges limits on access to failing code, and follows up after discovering the relevant dependency.
